title: Can a small VHE model overfit cached pairs and improve dev loss in a short run?
hypothesis: A ResidualUNet with 16 channels can drive the humanization loss down on a fixed batch of 8 cached pairs, and a 400-step random-crop run on the aligned train cache lowers the dev loss relative to its own initial value, with output length and sample rate preserved.
command: cd ~/VHE && .venv/bin/python -m vhe train --cache ~/datasets/VHE-Datasets/derived/aishell3-pairs/p2-train40x10-v2 --output .../aishell3-runs/EXP-0025-overfit8 --overfit 8 --steps 60 --batch-size 8 --channels 16 --crop-s 1.6 --learning-rate 3e-4 --checkpoint-every 20 --log-every 5 --device cuda --seed 42 || same with --output .../EXP-0025-400 --dev-cache .../p2-dev12x5-v2 --steps 400 --batch-size 4 --eval-every 50 --checkpoint-every 100 --log-every 20
notes: Two arms. Arm A (overfit 8 pairs, 60 steps, lr 3e-4) failed its preregistered 0.6x criterion at 0.914x; arm B (400 steps, lr 3e-4, random crops, 217 pairs) lowered dev total 3.4554 -> 3.2451 over 4 evaluations. Three pipeline failures preceded the runs and are kept in README: missing backend (369/369 + 60/60 rejected, backend_inventory_insufficient), wrong backend name ('mandarin' vs 'mandarin_formant', KeyError), and missing --eval-batches CLI flag (argparse error). Failed caches derived/aishell3-pairs/p2-train40x10 and p2-dev12x5 are retained unmodified. GPU peak memory was not instrumented in these runs. No listening test.
command_provenance: reconstructed from the effective TrainConfig stored in the run's checkpoint sidecar (checkpoints/step-XXXXXX.json); the remote shell did not persist history, so the literal argv is not recoverable
